{
 "summary": "Findings (I confirmed each one by running a scratch probe against the real modules with bun. No files were changed.)

1. Title: Refund adds the processing fee a second time and pays back more than was charged
Severity: P1
Location: billing.ts:88 (also 96)
Failure: The refund should reverse the charge exactly. `charge.grossCents` already includes the fee (types.ts doc; billing.ts:64), but `refund` runs `applyProcessingFee(charge.grossCents)` on it again. Probe: an EUR charge of gross 1120 produced a refund of gross -1152. Every refund overpays by about 2.9% of the charge.
Fix: Use `grossCents: -charge.grossCents`. Do not recompute the amount from the charge.

2. Title: Refund converts at today's FX rate instead of the rate captured on the charge
Severity: P1
Location: billing.ts:89-90, 97-98
Failure: `refund` calls `this.rates.current(charge.currency)` and settles again. Rates change over time (rates.ts:3-4), so the refund's settled USD does not match the charge's. Probe: charge settled at 1232 (rate 1.10); after the rate moved to 1.20 the refund settled at -1382. The ledger no longer nets to zero, and the stored `fxRate` does not describe the charge being reversed. This is one Single Source of Truth problem with finding 1: the refund recomputes values that the charge entry already holds.
Fix: Build the refund from the charge entry: `settledCents: -charge.settledCents` and `fxRate: charge.fxRate`. Remove the rate lookup and the `settle` call from `refund`. If FX gain or loss on refunds is a real requirement, record it as a separate entry.

3. Title: Refund is not idempotent, so one charge can be refunded many times
Severity: P1
Location: billing.ts:82-103; ledger.ts:13
Failure: `refund` sets `idempotencyKey: refund:${charge.id}` but never calls `findByIdempotencyKey` before appending. Probe: calling `refund(c.id)` twice posted two refunds (led_2 and led_3). `Ledger.append` then silently replaces the earlier key mapping in `byKey`. A retried refund request pays out again.
Fix: At the top of `refund`, return the existing entry when `findByIdempotencyKey(\`refund:${chargeId}\`)` finds one. Have `Ledger.append` throw on a duplicate key instead of overwriting.

4. Title: The idempotency key is built from purchase contents, not request identity: different purchases merge, and retries across midnight double-charge
Severity: P1
Location: billing.ts:42-46, 58-61
Failure: The key is `customerId:currency:subtotal:utcDay` and ignores `request.requestId`, line items and promo.
(a) Two different purchases on the same day with the same subtotal share a key. Probe: a 1000-cent item and 2x500-cent items returned the same entry (`c===c2` was true), so the second purchase is never charged and the caller is told it succeeded.
(b) A retry that crosses UTC midnight gets a new day bucket and is charged again, which is the double charge this change is meant to stop.
(c) A replay with a different promo or currency quietly returns the original entry.
The comment's claim that the day bucket "keeps the key space bounded" is false: `byKey` never evicts, so the bucket only adds the midnight bug.
Fix: Key on the client-supplied `request.requestId`, scoped by customer. Remove the day bucket. Optionally keep a hash of the request body and reject a replay whose body differs.

5. Title: Fixed-amount promo charges tax on the pre-discount subtotal, unlike percent promos
Severity: P2
Location: billing.ts:34-36
Failure: The percent path taxes the discounted amount (lines 29-31). The fixed path taxes the full subtotal and subtracts the discount afterwards. Probe: a 1000-cent fixed promo on a 1000-cent subtotal gives tax 88 and total 88, so the customer pays tax on a free order. A percent promo of 100 gives total 0. Two promos worth the same amount produce different totals and different recorded tax.
Fix: One path: compute `discountCents` (by percent or fixed, clamped to `[0, subtotal]`), then `discounted = subtotal - discount`, then `tax = round(discounted * TAX_RATE)`. The three branches collapse into one, which also fixes the duplicated tax code.

6. Title: Promo value is never validated; out-of-range values give negative totals or surcharges
Severity: P2 (P1 if `ChargeRequest` comes straight from the client, which the "client retries" comment at billing.ts:39 suggests: UNVERIFIED, since the repo has no caller to check)
Location: billing.ts:28-35; types.ts:10-15
Failure: The types.ts doc says percent values are 0-100, but nothing enforces it. Probe: percent 150 produced discount 1500, tax -44, total -544. That negative total is then charged and settled as a negative amount. A negative fixed value is not caught by `Math.min`, so it raises the total. The request also carries the `PromoCode` object itself (`kind` and `value`), so whoever builds the request decides the discount. The `code` string is never looked up anywhere.
Fix: Look up the promo on the server from `code`. Clamp or reject a percent value outside [0,100], and a fixed value that is negative or not an integer.

7. Title: Reconciliation compares float dollar sums with `!==` and will page finance on-call when nothing is wrong
Severity: P1
Location: reconcile.ts:5-11, 17-18
Failure: `statementTotalDollars` adds `settledCents / 100` as binary floats, and `reconcile` compares the result exactly to `processorBalanceCents / 100`. Probe: entries of 10 and 20 cents against a balance of 30 reported a discrepancy (`computedDollars: 0.30000000000000004`). This breaks the function's own stated rule that it "must never fire spuriously".
Fix: Sum integer `settledCents` and compare to `processorBalanceCents` as integers. Make `Discrepancy` carry `computedCents` instead of the mixed-unit `computedDollars` (types.ts:53-56). Convert to dollars only when formatting for display.

8. Title: No tests for any of the new money, FX or idempotency behavior
Severity: P2
Location: whole change (the project has no test files)
Failure: Every defect above (refund fee, refund FX, double refund, key collision, promo tax, float reconcile) could be caught by a one-line assertion and none exists. Each one reproduced on the first try.
Fix: Add behavioral tests:
- charge then refund nets to zero in both gross and settled amounts, including when the rate changes in between;
- a refund retry returns the same entry;
- two different `requestId`s with the same subtotal create two charges, and a replay across midnight does not create a second one;
- fixed and percent promos of equal value produce the same total and tax;
- `reconcile` returns null for amounts like 10+20 vs 30.

9. Title: Minor naming and doc problems
Severity: P3
Location: reconcile.ts:24; billing.ts:107; billing.ts:9
Failure:
- The docstring example on reconcile.ts:24 shows a charge as "-$10.40", but charges are positive.
- `settle(grossCents, ...)` (billing.ts:107) and the `*Cents` fields hold whole yen for JPY, which misleads readers. The `settle` comment explains this instead of the names carrying it (Comments-as-Apology).
- billing.ts:9 claims the fee function is "Correct for any net amount", but the refund applies it to an amount that already includes the fee.
Fix: Fix the example. Rename the fields to `grossMinor`/`settledMinorUsd` (or similar) so the unit is in the name.

Notes, not defects:
- The charge path captures the FX rate correctly: one rate is read once and stored on the entry (billing.ts:65-66).
- Settlement converts the JPY scale correctly (minorUnitsPerMajor(JPY)=1).
- Check-then-append in `charge` has no race, because synchronous JS runs it on one thread.",
 "files_modified": []
}

 "summary": "Findings (I confirmed each behavior with bun probes in /tmp/rv/p.ts and /tmp/rv/q.ts against the real modules; no repo files modified):

P1 - Permission invalidation skips the stale tier. cache.ts:72-83: invalidatePrefix clears only `fresh` and `empty`. An entry older than 30s has already moved to `stale` (cache.ts:35-36), so it keeps being served (and revalidated) for up to 150s after access is revoked. Probe: set, age 40s, get, invalidatePrefix, then get returned {kind:"stale", value:["revoked"]}. Fix: also clear `stale`. Better: merge to one map and derive freshness from age (see the Single Source of Truth finding below).

P1 - An in-flight fetch repopulates the cache after invalidation. api.ts:59-60 (miss path) and api.ts:67-70 (revalidate) call store() when a fetch started before onPermissionsChanged (api.ts:83-85) resolves, so pre-revocation rows get written back as a fresh 30s hit. Probe: start a list, invalidate, resolve with the revoked doc, and the cache key reads "hit". Fix: keep a per-viewer generation counter, capture it before the fetch, and skip store() if it changed. Also make invalidation clear or neutralize `revalidating` entries for that viewer.

P1 - Cursors are not bound to the requesting viewer. api.ts:22-23 and cursor.ts:20-26: resolveCursor returns the stored query, including the issuer's viewerId, and list() never compares it with request.viewerId. Probe: viewer "attacker" passing victim's nextCursor received victim's docs [secret2, s3]. This contradicts the cursor.ts:8-9 claim that clients cannot reach "another viewer's query". Tokens are also guessable: a sequential counter plus 8 chars of non-crypto Math.random (cursor.ts:15). Fix: reject when state.query.viewerId !== request.viewerId and generate tokens with crypto.randomUUID().

P1 - Shared cursor state is mutated in place. api.ts:38 does `state.offset += items.length` on the object stored in the `live` map (cursor.ts:16, 25), and api.ts:39 registers that same object under the new token. Every token in a chain aliases one PageState. Retrying or reusing a cursor skips data, and concurrent use corrupts it. Probe: reusing page 1's nextCursor returned [d2,d3] first, then [d4,d5]. Fix: treat PageState as immutable and issue `{ query: state.query, offset: state.offset + items.length }` as a new object.

P1 - Negative-cache TTL unit mismatch. cache.ts:62-63: `ageSeconds` is already in seconds but is compared with `NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS * 1000`, so empty results stay cached for 5000s (~83 min) instead of 5s. A viewer who gets new documents, or a page that fills later, keeps seeing [] with zero source calls. Probe: 60s later the page was still empty and the source was not called. Fix: compare `ageSeconds < NEGATIVE_TTL_SECONDS`, or keep milliseconds on both sides as get() does.

P1 - Cache key omits includeArchived. api.ts:7-8: the key is viewerId:sort:filter:offset:pageSize, but Query now carries includeArchived (types.ts:36) and the source filters on it. An includeArchived=true page is then served for an includeArchived=false request, and the reverse. Probe: "archived leak: true". Fix: add includeArchived to the key. Better: build the key from every Query field in one place so new fields cannot be missed.

P2 - Negative and positive tiers are not kept mutually exclusive. cache.ts:48-57: markEmpty leaves existing fresh/stale rows in place, and set() does not delete the `empty` entry. When a stale page revalidates to empty (api.ts:74-75), the old rows survive in `stale`. Once the negative TTL lapses (with the unit bug fixed), get() resurrects rows that the source said no longer exist, possibly revoked or deleted docs, and serves them as "stale". Fix: markEmpty deletes fresh/stale, and set deletes empty. Better: one map whose entries are a discriminated value-or-empty union.

P2 - Off-by-one at the last page. api.ts:35: `hasMore = items.length >= pageSize` reports hasMore=true and issues a cursor when the last page is exactly full. The next request returns an empty page, which is also negative-cached for 83 min because of the TTL bug. Probe: 6 docs with pageSize 3 gave page 2 hasMore=true and page 3 empty. Fix: fetch pageSize+1 rows, return pageSize, and set hasMore from the extra row. The cache key and fetch limit must use the same limit.

P2 - Background revalidation failures become unhandled rejections. api.ts:67-70: `void fetch().then(store).finally(...)` has no catch. A source error rejects the detached promise, which can terminate a Bun or Node process under default settings. Probe: "unhandledRejection: boom". Fix: add .catch that logs once and keeps the stale entry.

P2 - Unbounded server-side memory. cursor.ts:10 and 16: issueCursor runs on every page that has more results. releaseCursor (cursor.ts:29) has no callers, and nothing expires tokens, despite the "expired" wording at cursor.ts:23. Every paginated listing leaks a PageState forever. The cache maps (cache.ts:22-24) only delete on access of the same key, so never-reread keys accumulate. The cache.ts:19-20 claim that the stale tier "bounds" churn is false: there is no size bound. Fix: give cursors a TTL and size cap (or a signed stateless cursor carrying viewerId, query and offset). Cap or sweep the cache maps.

P2 - includeArchived is labeled "Admin-only" (types.ts:16-17) but api.ts:29 passes request.includeArchived through with no authorization check. UNVERIFIED: whether DocumentSource.fetch enforces admin status. types.ts:27-28 says it enforces only per-viewer permissions. Fix: authorize at the API boundary or document that the source enforces it.

P2 - Single Source of Truth / Parallel State in SwrCache. cache.ts:22-24: three maps hold mutually exclusive states of one key, and the fresh-to-stale move (cache.ts:35-36) is Manual Sync of a value derivable from storedAt. This structure directly causes the invalidation hole (stale skipped), the empty/positive overlap, and the inconsistent unit handling between get() and isKnownEmpty(). Fix: one Map<string, {value: T | EMPTY, storedAt}>, with hit/stale/empty classified from age at read time and a single delete-by-prefix.

P2 - Missing tests. The diff adds no tests for cache aging, negative TTL, invalidation across tiers, cursor reuse, cross-viewer cursors, or the last-page boundary. Every P1 above would have been caught by a small test with a fake clock.

P3 - Keys are colon-delimited with unescaped fields. api.ts:8 and 84: a viewerId containing ':' can collide with another viewer's key; for example, viewer "a:updated"/sort title/filter F and viewer "a"/sort updated/filter "title:F" produce the same key. invalidatePrefix("a:") also wipes viewer "a:..." entries. UNVERIFIED: whether viewer ids can contain ':'. Fix: escape or JSON-encode the key components.

P3 - Offset cursors over independently cached pages mix snapshots. api.ts:34 with api.ts:52-57: page N may come from a 150s-old stale entry while page N+1 is fetched live, so inserts or deletes in between cause duplicated or skipped documents across pages. Fix: use keyset cursors (last sort key plus id), or document this as accepted.

P3 - Request fields are silently ignored when a cursor is present. api.ts:22-23: filter, sort and includeArchived on the request are dropped in favor of the stored query, with no error if they differ. Fix: reject mismatches or document that only pageSize applies.

P3 - The error message echoes the cursor token. cursor.ts:23: `Unknown or expired cursor: ${token}` puts a bearer-like token into errors and logs. Fix: omit the token.

P3 - Units of CacheClock.now() are undocumented. types.ts:39-41: cache.ts assumes milliseconds (the *1000 conversions), but the interface does not say so. Fix: document that it returns epoch milliseconds, or rename it to nowMs().",
 "files_modified": []
}

 "summary": "Findings: the plan cannot be implemented as written. Four of its central premises are false against the snapshot, plus a nonexistent version target and wrong packaging behavior.

1. P1, false baseline: @opentui/core is already 0.5.1. Plan context.key_files[0], phase-1 t1, and success_criteria[0] all say core is at 0.2.15 and "must rise to 0.5.1". Evidence: package.json:90 `"@opentui/core": "0.5.1"`, package.json:91 `"@opentui/solid": "0.5.1"`. The lockstep already holds, so the "raise core" edit does nothing. Fix: drop the manifest edit from t1, and keep only the ledger assertion if it is still wanted.

2. P1, misread fixture: binary-native-assets.test.ts does not "exercise the current 0.2.15". Plan key_files[2] and phase-1 t1 claim it does. Evidence: tests/unit/scripts/binary-native-assets.test.ts:68 declares core 0.5.1 with optionalDependency core-win32-x64 0.5.1. Line 73 stages a stale core-win32-x64 at 0.2.15 on purpose, and line 78 expects a replacement with 0.5.1. So 0.2.15 is the deliberately mismatched input, not the current pin. That file needs no edit. Fix: remove it from phase-1 files and t1.files, and keep it only as a regression check.

3. P1, the ledger file and its green baseline do not exist. Plan constraints[0] says "bun test tests/unit/scripts/dependency-pins.test.ts ran green ... every pin-ledger assertion passed". key_files[1] and the phase-1 goal say t1 "extends" it. d1 and success_criteria[4] say it "stays green ... as it was before the plan". Evidence: tests/unit/scripts/ holds 23 files (manifest, binary-native-assets, opentui-native-package-patch, release-*, check-*, ...) and no dependency-pins.test.ts. No test references web-tree-sitter pins or the opentui/solid lockstep. Bun also fails when given a nonexistent test path, so the phase-1 verification command fails as written. Fix: restate the work as creating a new ledger, with RED evidence and no claimed baseline. Remove "extends a proven contract".

4. P1, OpenAI is not pinned exactly. Plan key_files[0], constraints[3], phase-1 t2 description and scenario, and success_criteria[2] all say openai is "already pinned exactly at 6.39.0", so it is "out of scope". Evidence: package.json:102 `"openai": "^6.39.0"`, a caret range that floats across 6.x. This is exactly the reproducibility gap the plan is meant to close, and the plan explicitly forbids fixing it. Fix: put openai in t2, pin it to the version the lockfile actually resolves (that resolved version is unverified here because there is no bun.lock in the snapshot), and add a ledger assertion.

5. P1, web-tree-sitter 0.25.12 does not exist, and the bump breaks the peer pin. Phase-2 t1, d2, and success_criteria[1] want "0.25.12, the final patch release of the 0.25 line". Evidence from npm (https://registry.npmjs.org/web-tree-sitter): the 0.25.x line is 0.25.0 through 0.25.10, with 0.26.x after it. So 0.25.10 is the last 0.25 patch, and a "fresh install resolves 0.25.12" cannot happen. Also, https://registry.npmjs.org/@opentui/core/0.5.1 declares `peerDependencies: {"web-tree-sitter": "0.25.10"}` (exact), which matches the hold rationale at package.json:85. Any move off 0.25.10 contradicts the manifest note and the core 0.5.1 peer contract. Fix: drop phase 2. web-tree-sitter is already at the end of its line. A ledger assertion that it equals @opentui/core's peer pin would be the useful guard.

6. P1, releasing.md is not shipped in the .vsix. Phase-3 t1 claims "The published .vsix ships the whole vscode/docs directory next to docs/about-flywheel.md". d3 and success_criteria[3] build on that claim. Evidence: vscode/.vscodeignore:7 excludes `docs/**`, and :8-10 re-include only `!docs/about-flywheel.md`, which the comment there calls "the one docs file the extension opens at runtime". So the d3 check ("packaged extension lists docs/releasing.md") and the qualitative verification fail. The plan never lists .vscodeignore as a file to edit. The design point is also wrong: releasing.md is a maintainer runbook (vscode/docs/releasing.md:36-60 covers publisher PATs, `vsce login`, tag recovery) and has no place in a user package. Fix: keep releasing.md out of the package, delete d3, the "installed users read it offline" rationale, the inventory scenario, and the install-and-open UAT, and verify the runbook edit as a doc change only.

7. P2, phase-3 verification proves nothing about inventory and cannot be confirmed. `cd vscode && bun run package darwin-arm64` builds a package but lists no files. Also, the snapshot has no vscode/package.json, so the package script cannot be confirmed (vscode/ contains only .vscodeignore and docs/). If any inventory check stays, it needs `vsce ls` or `unzip -l` on the .vsix.

8. P2, t2 is unspecified. It says "Convert the floating runtime ranges the audit marks for exactness" but names no audit and no list. The floating runtime ranges are package.json:92 @solid-primitives/keyed ^1.5.3, :98 fuzzysort ^3.1.0, :99 highlight.js ^11.11.1, :100 js-yaml ^4.1.1, :102 openai ^6.39.0, :103 partial-json ^0.1.7, and :104 sharp ^0.35.3. The scenarios cover only the holds (marked, web-tree-sitter, openai), so an implementer cannot tell what to change. sharp needs care: binary-native-assets.test.ts:69-75 stages sharp 0.35.3 natives, and the patterns rule "exact pins for runtime deps whose native graphs move in lockstep" applies to it directly. Fix: list each entry and its target exact version, taken from the lockfile.

9. P2, the "rejects divergent manifest" scenario forces a seam the plan never designs. A ledger that reads the real package.json cannot show rejection of a diverging manifest unless the check is a pure function over a manifest object. The plan names no such function or where it lives. Fix: define a small pure checker fed by both the real manifest and a fixture, or drop that scenario.

10. P2, the ledger misses the real coupling. The rationale for the exact pins is the @opentui/core 0.5.1 dependency graph (npm: dependencies diff 9.0.0, marked 17.0.1, string-width 7.2.0, plus the web-tree-sitter 0.25.10 peer). These match package.json:96, :101, :106, :107. Calling marked a vague "deliberate hold" (constraints[2]) misses this. Fix: have the ledger assert these mirror @opentui/core's declared versions. That replaces several restated-constant assertions with one derived rule (Single Source of Truth).

11. P3, phase-2 verification does not test the change. opentui-native-package-patch.test.ts tests import rewriting (tests/unit/scripts/opentui-native-package-patch.test.ts:1-40), and binary-native-assets.test.ts does not cover the web-tree-sitter version. Neither can catch a bad web-tree-sitter bump. Moot if phase 2 is dropped.

12. P3, a project doc is missing. context.project_docs lists AGENTS.md, but there is no AGENTS.md in the snapshot.

13. P3, there is no lockfile in the snapshot (no bun.lock), so the "fresh install resolves ..." scenarios and resolved versions cannot be checked from the repo. Any exact pins must come from a real lockfile or an install.

Verified: package.json lines cited; .vscodeignore:7-10; the binary-native-assets fixture at :59-83; the contents of the test tree; the npm registry version list for web-tree-sitter; the @opentui/core 0.5.1 deps and peer pin. Unverified: the resolved openai version, and whether vscode's package script exists.",
 "files_modified": []
}

 "summary": "Findings: (verified in a scratch copy with diff.patch applied, using bun test)

1. Title: The nightly backfill silently skips payout.settled. Severity: P1. Location: backfill.ts:8 (BACKFILLED_KINDS, which the diff does not touch) and the skip branch at backfill.ts:16-18. Failure: The registry.ts:17-18 comment says both production consumers read PRODUCTION_VALIDATORS. But backfill only replays kinds listed in BACKFILLED_KINDS, which still contains only order.placed, order.cancelled and refund.issued. Probe: a valid payout.settled event gets {status:"accepted"} from ingestEvent, while runBackfill([e]) returns {accepted:[],invalid:[],skipped:["p1"]}. So payouts missed during a webhook outage are never recovered. They are also never reported as failures, because "skipped" means "kind this service never consumes" (backfill.ts:4-7, types.ts:25), which is now wrong for payouts. The live path works and the recovery path does not. Single Source of Truth: the set of handled kinds lives in two places (the registry and BACKFILLED_KINDS), kept in step by hand, and the diff updated only one. Fix: add "payout.settled" to BACKFILLED_KINDS (backfill.ts:8). Better: derive the replayed set from the registry keys, or from one list that both consumers use, so adding a kind cannot leave backfill behind.

2. Title: The added test never touches the production registry or either production consumer. Severity: P2. Location: payout.test.ts:6 (and :8-20). Failure: The test builds its own registry with createValidatorRegistry([payoutSettledValidator]), so "the registry resolves payout.settled" only checks a registry made inside the test. It would pass with the registry.ts:23 change removed. Probe: after deleting payoutSettledValidator from PRODUCTION_VALIDATORS, payout.test.ts still passed 3/3. Without that line, live ingest would reject every payout with "no validator registered". The test also cannot catch finding 1, because it never calls ingestEvent or runBackfill. Tests 2-3 just call the validator through a lookup that adds nothing; they check validator logic, not wiring. Fix: test through the real entrypoints in registry.test.ts, which already owns the ingest and backfill tests. Add a valid and an invalid payout.settled case to the "live ingest" describe. Add a payout.settled event to the backfill test "replays every kind the job is configured for" (registry.test.ts:25-33), which asserts accepted and skipped=[]. That test would fail today and expose finding 1. Then drop or shrink payout.test.ts so it does not duplicate them.

3. Title: The payout.settled validator's missing-field checks are only partly tested. Severity: P3. Location: payout.test.ts:17-20. Failure: Only a missing currency is tested. A non-positive or non-integer amountCents and a missing payoutId are untested. This is minor because the shared helpers (validators.ts:3-11) are already exercised by refund.issued (registry.test.ts:35-38). Fix: optionally add one case with amountCents <= 0 through ingestEvent.

Notes:
- The validator itself (validators.ts, the added lines) and the EventKind union change (types.ts:1) are correct, and the duplicate-kind guard is not triggered.
- Currency is only checked to be a non-empty string; it is not checked against a currency-code format. That matches the existing project style and is not a finding unless the provider contract requires more (not verified, since there is no spec here).",

 "summary": "Review of the multi-path terminal drop change (src/tui/hooks/composer-attachments.ts, tests/unit/tui/hooks/prompt-attachments.test.ts, PI-INTERACTION-031). Result: one P3 elegance finding. I found no correctness defects and no intent drift.

Findings:

Title: Parity-encoded split array leaks from pasteParts into claimPasteText
Severity: P3
Location: src/tui/hooks/composer-attachments.ts:32-40, src/tui/hooks/composer-attachments.ts:367-371
Failure: Narrow Interfaces, Deep Modules. The candidate and separator split should be owned by one function, so that the caller only iterates over text parts and path parts. pasteParts returns a flat string[] whose meaning depends on index parity: separators sit at even indexes and candidates at odd ones. It also returns the sentinel `["", text]` only to keep that parity. claimPasteText must repeat the encoding (`index % 2 === 1`, line 368) and then build a second mixed `string | {paths,text}` array. The docstring at 32-35 exists to explain this encoding. The same knowledge now lives in two places, and a future edit to either one breaks the other silently.
Fix: Let pasteParts take cwd and return the classified parts directly: `readonly (string | { paths: readonly string[]; text: string })[]`, which applies pathText and the IMAGE_PATH check per candidate inside itself. Or inline the split into claimPasteText. claimPasteText then reads `const parts = pasteParts(text, cwd); if (parts.every(isString)) return false; ...`, with no parity arithmetic.

Assigned claims (verified):
- Claim 1, "a single path behaves exactly as before": TRUE as stated. src/tui/hooks/composer-attachments.ts:39 returns ["", text] unless 2 or more candidates all pass isAbsolute. In that case line 368 calls pathText(text) on the whole paste, as the old code did. The inserted text is "" + marker, so the result is the same as the old insertText(marker). I ran a scratch probe of pasteParts (bun): "/a/My Shot.png", "/a.png ", "/a.png" and "/a.png\\" each gave ["", text]. " /a.png /b.png " split into [" ","/a.png"," ","/b.png"," "].    - Location: tests/helpers/real-process-fixture.ts:391-395 and :418-424.
   - Failure: harnessProcesses decides a match from one table read (time T0). stopHarnessProcesses then calls `identifyProcess(entry.pid)` (time T1) and kills whatever has that pid at T1. `killIdentifiedProcess` only compares T1 to T2, so nothing ties the identity to the process that was matched at T0.

For a retried job, the listener overwrites the saved retry copy (new attempt and runAt) with the stale original, which is due immediately. Probe: a job that was done before stop was pending after stop. Fix: remove the listener in `finally` for every outcome (or use `{ once: true }` plus a finally removal). The comment's reason ("before the handler could report progress") does not apply, because `attempt` counts completed attempts, not progress. Probe: a job at attempt 3 that timed out was saved as pending with attempt 0. Fix: delete the special case. JobTimeoutError already has `transient = true`, so the general path at lines 92-95 retries it with a bounded count and growing backoff.

From then on nothing is written, `pending` grows without limit, and dispose() rejects. Probe: after the first sink error, the sink was called once in total and wrote `[]`; there were 2 unhandled rejections and dispose threw. Fix: chain flushes as `this.inflight = (this.inflight ??
